args.root_cause: Config deploy for ticket OPS-250 (deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md) pushed a server.properties that, besides the intended max-players 20->40, also set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true while whitelist.json was empty ([]). The deploy restarted the server (stop at 06:53:06, back up ~06:54:30), which disconnected Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines; on restart every join attempt (Alex_Builds, Steve_Mines, newplayer09, newplayer10) was rejected with "You are not whitelisted on this server!".
args.actions: 1) Took baseline status/logs and snapshotted server.properties at shift start. 2) Noticed stale exporter metrics, then status DOWN; found deploy note and diffed current server.properties against my snapshot and deploy/previous/server.properties: white-list and enforce-whitelist had flipped to true in addition to max-players=40. 3) Confirmed whitelist.json was empty; declared the incident. 4) While the server was mid-restart, wrote server.properties = previous config + max-players=40 (white-list=false, enforce-whitelist=false). The boot had already loaded the bad properties, so on coming up it still rejected players. 5) Ran console `whitelist off` (reply: "Whitelist is now turned off"), which fixed the live state without another restart; players began joining 2 s later. 6) The server's rewrite of server.properties on that command restored enforce-whitelist=true, so I rewrote server.properties once more with enforce-whitelist=false, white-list=false, max-players=40. 7) Verified: no whitelist rejections after 06:54:40, joins resumed from 06:54:44 (Steve_Mines, Alex_Builds, newplayer11-22), TPS 20, 2 players online, on-disk config correct. I did not stop or restart the server myself; the one restart was performed by the deploy before I intervened.
args.residual_risk: Players lost their session during the deploy's restart and were locked out for ~15 s after boot. The deploy tooling that pushed the wrong file is unchanged and could re-push a bad server.properties; the deploy note and deploy/previous/ remain as-is for the team. If anyone runs a whitelist toggle command before the next restart, Paper will rewrite server.properties from its in-memory copy (enforce-whitelist=true) — harmless while the whitelist is off, and the on-disk file I wrote will be read correctly on the next restart. The 4 end_crystal/strider etc. entities and offline-mode warnings are pre-existing and unrelated.
